messages:
Anna G: Hey team — SparrowBoard asked for a coordinated perf run next week. Goal: 3-day perf/W + throughput sweep, plus a kernel-tune pass. Can we confirm what we (Redwood) need to hand off and who owns which artifacts?

Mike T: I can own the model config + inference recipe. Thinking we should provide 3 model sizes (base, med, large) and fixed seq lengths: 512/1024/2048. Will that match their lab runs?

Sophia L: Yep that set maps to their slot bins. Also we should provide prompt templates and a small eval set so we can compare quality vs quant configs. I recommend adding latency p50/p95 targets for each seq.

Raj P: For kernel tuning, SparrowBoard will want kernel symbols and perf counter hooks. We can give them a slimmed kernel build + symbols but not our internal debug flags. Legal cleared a minimal NDA addendum for telemetry.

Anna G: Good. Logistics checklist: 1) S3 bucket + perms for artifacts, 2) bench harness/docker image, 3) runbook with measurement definitions, 4) telemetry schema + sample traces. Who can produce the runbook?

Mike T: I'll draft the runbook. Proposed measurement defs include: throughput (tokens/s), perf/W (tokens/s per watt), latency percentiles, and KV cache warm/cold curves. I'll include the exact command lines.

Sophia L: I'll curate the eval prompt set and golden outputs for quality regression checks. Also adding an automated diff script to flag generation divergences > threshold.

Raj P: Bench-bot can provision telemetry tags. @bench-bot can you create a telemetry schema in the shared bucket with fields: run_id, model, seq_len, quant, kernel_version, avg_power_w, tokens_per_sec, p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms?

bench-bot: created telemetry-schema.json in s3://redwood-partner-data/sparrowboard/1747632100/telemetry-schema.json :white_check_mark:

Anna G: Nice. For the docker image: we should pin CUDA/cuDNN + kernel build hash in the run metadata so we can reproduce. Also add a small sanity test that runs a churned prompt through 10 steps to detect misbehaving fused kernels.

Mike T: Draft of run command I'm going to include in the runbook:

```bash
./run_infer.sh --model rdl-7b --seq 1024 --batch 1 --quant fp16 --measurements throughput,power,latency --out s3://redwood-partner-data/sparrowboard/1747632100/runs/rdl-7b-1024-1
```

Sophia L: FYI SparrowBoard asked to try INT8-quant on the med model as an experiment. We should include quality thresholds; if topk BLEU-like metric drops > 3 points we mark it failing.

Raj P: On kernel tuning: request they capture perf counters per kernel (kernel_name, duration_ms, cycles). We'll map hot kernels to potential fuse/stride fixes. Plan a triage call mid-run if we see anomalous power/latency regressions.

Anna G: Schedule: handoff Monday EOD, bench runs Tue-Thu, preliminary recap Fri morning. I'll set up a shared calendar invite and a Slack channel #sparrow-collab.

Mike T: I'll put the initial runbook + docker image link into the bucket by Mon 18:00 PT.

Sophia L: I'll upload prompts + diff script by Monday as well.

Raj P: I'll prepare the kernel symbol tar and the minimal kernel build instructions (no internal flags) and get legal to sign off on the telemetry NDA addendum.

Anna G: Great. One last thing — can we add a short README that maps our metric names to SparrowBoard's naming? They call 'power_eff' what we call perf_per_w. Small mapping avoids confusion.

Mike T: Will do.

Sophia L: :thumbsup:

bench-bot: reminder scheduled: "sparrowboard-run-start" at 1747718500 UTC — will post run start & end messages into #sparrow-collab :robot_face:

Anna G: Thanks everyone — syncing with SparrowBoard tomorrow to finalize run window. If anything blocks, ping here and I'll escalate. :v:
